source_text: Haec vobis scripsi per Crescentem, quem in praesenti commendavi vobis et nunc commendo. Conversatus est enim nobiscum inculpabiliter; credo quia et vobiscum similiter. Sororem autem eius habebitis commendatam, cum venerit ad vos. Incolumes estote in domino Iesu Christo in gratia cum omnibus vestris. Amen.
thought_title: Commendation of Crescens and final greeting
orientation: Polycarp is closing his letter by commending the letter carrier Crescens and his sister, then giving a final blessing.
pass_a_gloss: These things I wrote to you through Crescens, whom in the present I commended to you and now I commend. For he has lived with us blamelessly; I believe that also with you likewise. But his sister you will have commended, when she comes to you. Be safe in the Lord Jesus Christ in grace with all yours. Amen.

choices.why: Renders the Latin phrase literally as a temporal expression, matching the source's contrast between past and present commendation.
The Latin verb conversor here means to conduct oneself or live, and the perfect tense is kept as a completed action with present relevance.
The adverb directly corresponds to the Latin and matches the brief's description of Crescens as blameless.
The imperative of sum with the adjective incolumis is a standard closing wish for well-being, rendered literally.
Keeps the prepositional phrase literal, preserving the theological sense of being in God's grace.

pass_b_english: I have written these things to you through Crescens, whom I commended to you when he was with you before, and I commend him to you again now. He has lived among us blamelessly, and I believe he will do the same among you. You will also receive his sister as one commended to you when she comes to you. Be safe in the Lord Jesus Christ, in grace with all your people. Amen.
